Summit County government is one of the largest employers in the county and is an employer of choice. With nearly 3,000 employees, the Human Resources Department is responsible for recruiting a diverse and inclusive workforce, creating opportunities for employees to work in myriad career fields (i.e. animal control, sanitary and sewer services, administration or the medical examiner’s office). Summit County is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Employee Resources
My Brother's Keeper
The Human Resource Department performs a variety of functions that include the overall administration of the Executive’s Office human resources operations for all employees. Key service areas include recruiting, benefits administration, payroll administration, policy development and compliance, classification and compensation management, drug testing, position management, performance management, employee relations, employee engagement, training and development, HR reporting, records maintenance and workforce planning.

In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions in the County of Summit will be based on qualifications, merit, and abilities. The County of Summit provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, pregnancy, status as a parent, national origin, age, disability (physical or mental), family medical history or genetic information, political affiliation, military service, other non-merit based factors, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. (Ord.2004-596. Adopted 2-14-05; Ord. 2009-475. Adopted 11-30-09.) This applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.
